subject: Post-call: evaluation playbook & data checklist for Vetter Health
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@vetterhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04 15:12 PDT
Subject: Post-call: evaluation playbook & data checklist for Vetter Health

Lina — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our call so we can get your eval running on Redwood: 

1) Objective: run a 1k-case customer-specific eval focusing on summarization accuracy and hallucination rate for clinical discharge notes. Primary metric: factual precision at sentence-level; secondary: BLEU and a get-better qualitative score on hallucination cases.

2) Recommended model(s): start with RedLlama-13B-8q (low-latency, good for clinical NLG) as the control, and test RedLlama-33B-small-quant (higher-capacity variant) for quality delta. Ben will provide exact model strings and cost/latency estimates.

3) Data & format: we need 1,000 de-identified discharge notes in JSONL with fields: case_id, note_text, gold_summary. See attached sample and the vetter_eval_prompts.jsonl prompt set. Please confirm ETA for data and whether your security/compliance team requires a Private deployment for the run.

4) Scoring & rubric: we propose automated scoring (sentence factual precision via entity overlap + custom hallucination tagging) plus a 50-sample human review. Ben attached the benchmark CSV template for scorer outputs.

5) Timeline: once we receive data and a signed SOW, we can spin up a dedicated eval pod and deliver preliminary results in 5 business days.

Action items:
- Lina: confirm data delivery date and whether to use Hosted or Private (reply by EOD Thu).
- Vetter procurement: confirm we can proceed with the evaluation SOW (cc'd).
- Ben: supply model strings and expected token cost estimate.
- Marissa: prep the onboarding playbook and scoring pipeline runbook.

Attachments: vetter_eval_prompts.jsonl (prompt set), vetter_benchmark_template.csv (scoring template), redwood_eval_playbook_v1.pdf (onboarding runbook).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[hannah.schmitt@redwood.com]

From: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@vetterhealth.com>

Date: 2026-10-05 09:03 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call: evaluation playbook & data checklist for Vetter Health

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items: 

- We'll aim to deliver the 1,000 de-identified discharge notes by 2026-10-11. Our privacy team will remove direct PHI and provide the de-id checklist with the dataset.
- We want the eval to run in Private mode (VPC) because some notes still reference facility identifiers we prefer not to route through Hosted. I will loop in our infra security contact if you need network details.
- For the human review, we can provide two clinicians to annotate the 50-sample audit set; they'll use your rubric but we may add one clinical-specific hallucination flag.

Question: is RedLlama-33B-small-quant supported in Private today or would that require a short model onboarding window?

I'll confirm procurement timelines; cc'd them here.

Thanks,
Lina
Lina Ortiz
Director, Clinical Data Science — Vetter Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@vetterhealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05 10:20 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call: evaluation playbook & data checklist for Vetter Health

Hi all — quick notes on the model availability and scoring pipeline: 

- Model strings (Private-compatible): 
  - redwood/redllama-13b-8q:tag=2026-09-optimized
  - redwood/redllama-33b-quant-small:tag=2026-09-compat (requires a 24-48 hr model stage on the Private control plane; no code change on your side).

- Cost/latency: estimate for 1k-case run (avg note length ~750 tokens): 
  - 13B-8q: ~0.9 USD per case across tokens + infra (estimate) — median latency 280ms per request with batching. 
  - 33B-quant-small: ~2.5 USD per case — median latency 450ms with higher variance.

- Scoring & rubric specifics (attached template):
  1) Sentence factual precision: automated entity-level overlap (precision/recall/F1) computed against gold_summary entities. Threshold: pass if precision >= 0.88.
  2) Hallucination rate: compute per-case hallucination flag where any hallucinated sentence exists; we report % cases with hallucination. Target: <6% for the control.
  3) BLEU and ROUGE for surface similarity (informational).
  4) Human review: clinicians mark "Critical Hallucination" vs "Minor Hallucination"; disagreements adjudicated by third annotator.

- Deliverables: grader CSV (see vetter_benchmark_template.csv) + a short write-up with sample failure cases and recommended prompt tweaks.

I'll queue the Private model stage once Lina confirms Private deployment and provides IP ranges. Hannah/Marissa — I'll hand off the cost breakdown and a small script to convert their JSONL into our scoring pipeline format.

Ben

Please have your data team run the validator and share errors if any. If it's easier, we can accept an initial small sample (50 cases) to validate the pipeline before the full upload.

Thanks,
Hannah

Hi team — quick operational note: once we have a validated 50-sample, expected onboarding timeline for the 1k run is: 

- Day 0: validate sample and stage models in Private control plane (if Lina confirms IP ranges). 
- Day 1: full dataset ingest & automated scoring run (overnight). 
- Day 2: human review (50 samples) + final report prep. 

Total: ~3 business days from validated sample and signed SOW. I'll also attach a small conversion helper (jsonl_to_scoring.py) in the onboarding folder on Drive. Lina — I'll share access to the Drive link after procurement confirms.

Looking forward — Marissa
